purpose: Validate the stored Hessian-vector product without requiring a second machine's BLAS summation order to reproduce identical bits. Preserve the earlier direct-auditor failure.
arithmetic: Finite IEEE binary64 operands, round-to-nearest, at most 2*n elementary operations per dot product; FMA or reassociation may reduce or reorder those operations. Reject unsupported dimensions, nonfinite operands and potential overflow.
absolute_rounding_allowance: eta=2^-1074 (one smallest positive binary64 value, conservatively bounding a subnormal rounding error)
exact_reference: Convert each stored binary64 operand to an exact Rational{BigInt}; form each row's exact dot product s and absolute product sum a without floating-point arithmetic.
bound: k=2*n; gamma=k*u/(1-k*u). Require k*u<1, a<floatmax(binary64)/2 and |stored_hvp_i-s_i|<=gamma*a_i+k*eta/(1-k*u), using exact rational comparisons.
derivation: Each multiplication/addition contributes a relative error bounded by u and, conservatively, an absolute subnormal error eta. Collecting at most k factors (1+delta) gives gamma_k; the geometric accumulation of absolute errors is at most k*eta/(1-k*u). Any summation order satisfying this model obeys the same bound. The range guard prevents intermediate overflow. No empirical safety multiplier is fitted.
unchanged: All producer checks, the 1e-11 profile/algebra target, 1e-7 derivative target, finite-difference steps, raw operands and all historical/production gate failures remain unchanged. This is a report-reader arithmetic fix, not a new accepted physical result.
tests: distinct legal summation orders on an exactly specified cancellation example
current local and CI report operands under the fixed rule
all altered-report and cached rejection/restoration controls
